top_cited_works.venue: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Fluids
top_cited_works.abstract: SUMMARY After several years of planning, the 1st International Workshop on High‐Order CFD Methods was successfully held in Nashville, Tennessee, on January 7–8, 2012, just before the 50th Aerospace Sciences Meeting. The American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics, the Air Force Office of Scientific Research, and the German Aerospace Center provided much needed support, financial and moral. Over 70 participants from all over the world across the research spectrum of academia, government labs, and private industry attended the workshop. Many exciting results were presented. In this review article, the main motivation and major findings from the workshop are described. Pacing items requiring further effort are presented. Copyright © 2013 John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.

recent_works.title: The Effect of Thin-Layer Swirl on Turbulent Jet Mixing and Noise
recent_works.abstract: The effect of thin-layer swirl on the evolution of subsonic turbulent jet is investigated. The linear spatial stability analysis is used to estimate spatial amplitudes and phases of instability waves in an inviscid jet for different azimuthal modes, m=±1,±2,and ±3, and swirl number, S. For low and moderate swirl strength, negative helical modes are more unstable as compared to the positive counterparts, and the trend is reversed for higher swirl strength jets. High-order Implicit LES was used to verify the effect of thin-layer swirl on mixing and on noise mitigation. The thin-layer swirl is introduced at the nozzle exit by twelve vanes that impart angular momentum to the shear layer. Three additional nozzle configurations with azimuthally varying exit swirl were designed to study the effect of swirl modulation on mixing. The simulation results show that the thin-layer swirl promotes jet mixing in the near-field with uniform swirl performing higher mixing than swirl modulated jets.

recent_works.title: A Time-Accurate Dynamic Mesh Approach For High-Order Shock Computation in Multiple Dimensions
recent_works.abstract: A high-order shock-fitting approach has been developed for the two-dimensional Euler equations to compute shock waves with high-order accuracy. A time-accurate dynamic mesh algorithm plays a central role in the approach. A key ingredient of the strategy is a shock detection procedure capable of handling moving shock waves in a high-order simulation. Once shock waves are detected along element interfaces, the shock speed is computed based on the method of characteristics. Then, these interfaces move at the speed of the shock, and an upwind flux for the interfaces automatically guarantees the Rankine-Hugoniot condition. In addition, the entire mesh is deformed to comply with the motion of the shocks to avoid mesh warping and negative Jacobians. In the present study, quadratic (Q2) triangular meshes are employed. This means curved shocks are approximated with quadratic curves, achieving 3rd-order accuracy. The shock-fitting approach is tested for several benchmark problems to demonstrate its performance and accuracy.

recent_works.title: The Spatio-Temporal Behavior of a Passively Controlled E423 Airfoil Using an Equilateral Triangular Trip
recent_works.abstract: An investigation of the spatio-temporal dynamics of a passively tripped micro-scale Eppler E423 airfoil at two different temporal states was carried out using high-order large eddy simulation (LES). The tested temporal states were: startup using a freestream initial condition and quasi-steady state. The Reynolds number based on the chord was 40,000 and the angle of attack was 5◦. To provide a holistic understanding of the spatio-temporal dynamics that occur at both temporal states, metrics such as time histories, power spectral density (PSD) spectrums, and dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) spectrums were analyzed. It was found that the baseline configuration suffered from a low-frequency growth and decay of the primary laminar separation bubble (LSB). This led to poor aerodynamic performance for the baseline E423. However, it was shown that all of the tested tripped configurations with a trip height greater than 1×�� were successful in mitigating the formation of the primary (LSB), thus improving their aerodynamic performance significantly.

recent_works.title: High-Order Wall-Modeled Large Eddy Simulation of Benchmarks from the Hover Prediction Workshop
recent_works.abstract: In the present study, a high-order wall-modeled large eddy simulation (WMLES) tool called hpMusic is extended to handle dynamic moving grids and employed to tackle a benchmark problem from the AIAA Hover Prediction Workshop (HPW), flow over the HVAB Rotor. A p-refinement study is performed to assess the sensitivity of the computational results with respect to different solution polynomial orders, p = 3 and 4, called p3 and p4 simulations. In addition, the computational results are compared to other simulations in the literature and experimental data when possible to further verify and validate the present simulation methodology. The p4 simulations indeed captured more turbulent scales than the p3 simulations, and the computed figure of merit with p4 also agreed better with experimental data.

recent_works.title: High-Order Wall-Modeled LES of HLPW-5 Benchmarks
recent_works.abstract: This paper presents several mesh and order refinement studies of the benchmark problems from the 5th AIAA CFD High Lift Prediction Workshop (HLPW-5). A high-order large eddy simulation (LES) solver, hpMusic, was used in the present study. Recent developments in wall-modeled LES (WMLES) and GPU computing have made such simulations for high Reynolds number problems feasible within a reasonable amount of time. The present study pays special attention to the mesh and order sensitivity on the computational results. In addition, computational results are compared with experimental data when appropriate to further validate the present methodology.
